title: Trump critic Lula narrowly wins re-election in Brazil's presidential vote
summary: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, a vocal critic of U.S. President Donald Trump, was re-elected on Sunday.

image.caption: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva greets supporters in Sao Paulo on Sunday. (Tuane Fernandes/Reuters)

blocks.text: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, a vocal critic of U.S. President Donald Trump, was re-elected on Sunday.
Result keeps some distance between Latin America's biggest economy and Washington

Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, a vocal critic of U.S. President Donald Trump, was re-elected on Sunday in a result that keeps some distance between Latin America's biggest economy and Washington.
With 100 per cent of the vote counted, Brazil's electoral court announced that Lula, who turns 81 on Tuesday, held an unassailable lead.
The announcement capped an evening of chaos at polling places across Brazil, following a last-minute decision to extend voting by two hours.
That decision by a Supreme Court justice may trigger legal action by opponent Flávio Bolsonaro.

Lula's triumph bucks a trend in Latin America where increasing numbers of right-of-centre presidental candidates allied with Trump have been winning, further extending the United States' influence in the region.

Lula's victory leaves Mexico and Brazil, Latin America's two most populous nations, with left-of-centre leaders. It also positions the region's largest economy, with a GDP of $2.6 trillion US per year, to remain independent of the U.S., despite the pressure of increased tariffs imposed by Trump.
The announcement kicked off a celebration of supporters in and outside the Sao Paulo hotel where Lula watched the count with his wife, Rosângela da Silva, allies and friends.
His victory, if confirmed by electoral authorities, will give him his non-consecutive fourth term as president. The next term begins on Jan. 5, 2027.

It is the first time since Brazil's military dictatorship ended in 1985 that the second-highest vote getter in the first-round elections won the presidency. Bolsonaro had 47 per cent of the vote in the first round to Lula's 45 per cent, a difference of 2.2 million votes.
Lula and Bolsonaro, a senator and son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, have yet to address their supporters.
